purpose: One original painterly sky-only angular sector, intended for roughly 150–180 degrees of horizontal sky coverage, to raise useful source density relative to a full 360-degree panorama.
method: Built-in image_gen.imagegen; initial new generation using original panorama as palette/style reference, followed by one targeted imagegen edge-softening refinement. Only the second untouched generator PNG is selected.

calls.intent: New original artwork; reference supplied only for style/palette.

tool_arguments.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: ONE original sky-only angular-sector backdrop texture for a stylized painterly Godot coastal scene. This is artwork for a sky shader, not a screenshot, not a 360-degree equirectangular panorama.
Primary request: A richly articulated yet calm, hand-painted fair-weather coastal sky. Create a 2:1 landscape RGB image, requesting 4096 x 2048 pixels if available; otherwise keep the generator's native maximum dimensions. It represents one broad approximately 165-degree horizontal sky sector from the pale low horizon along the bottom toward higher blue sky at the top. Devote the pixels to clear sculptural cloud shapes with visible designed interior planes and crisp selectively softened silhouettes.
Style/medium: high-quality hand-painted animation background, soft gouache and oil-paint sensibility, broad confident brush planes; original artwork. The supplied image is a palette/style reference only, not an edit target. Keep its airy warm coastal daylight and its cream-and-blue cloud language, but compose a closer, substantially more detailed angular sector instead of a tiny cloud strip across a whole globe.
Composition/framing: Large luminous cumulus formations fill the middle-right and upper-right portion, contained comfortably inside the image; medium broken cumulus formations in the middle-left, also kept away from the outer edge. Arrange asymmetric varied large and medium forms, a few small connected wisps, and varied blue gaps. Keep a generous clear airy blue opening around center-left, approximately 28–47 percent across and 32–65 percent down, to leave space behind a pelican face that will be added separately by the game. DO NOT depict the pelican. The lower 12–18 percent is quiet pale blue/cyan atmospheric sky approaching the horizon, with only a few low faint soft clouds, no hard horizon stripe. Clouds should occupy enough height to show real layered volume, not a thin horizontal distant band. High sky stays open and airy.
Cloud forms: sunlit sculptural cumulus, coherent bright ivory and warm cream rims, large billowing lobes subdivided into deliberately painted medium-scale planes. Cool pale blue and muted lavender undersides with restrained tonal depth. Bright edges and colored shade must describe one coherent cloud mass rather than random marbling. A restrained variety of thin feathered cloud remnants connects or surrounds the principal forms.
Lighting/mood: clear sunny late-morning coastal daylight, welcoming, buoyant, gentle warm light from upper-left; no visible sun disk.
Color palette: blue sky similar to the reference, warm cream/ivory highlights, subtle pale peach warmth, cool blue-lavender cloud undersides, pale cyan-blue atmospheric bottom. Avoid saturated purple shadows or heavy gray clouds.
Edge handling: keep all important cloud masses away from the extreme left and right edges. Across the outermost 8–12 percent of both sides, clouds become progressively sparse and dissolve softly into open blue sky so a shader can feather the sector into a baseline sky. Left and right edges should have similar blue-to-pale-blue vertical color progression; exact seamless tiling is not required. No framing border.
Constraints: Entire image is sky and clouds only. No sea, no water, no land, no mountains, no buildings, no lighthouse, no birds, no characters, no objects, no sun disk, no lettering, no symbols, no text, no watermark. Do not render a finished game scene. No heavy storm clouds. No blurred haze smearing the cloud silhouettes. No noisy speckles, canvas grain, halftone, tiny procedural noise, repeated cloud pattern, or photographic microtexture. Preserve the painterly designed form.

calls.selection: Rejected as final because low cloud bases met both image edges.

calls.intent: Targeted edit to dissolve peripheral cloud bases and wisps into blue at the side edges while retaining central composition.

tool_arguments.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: original painterly sky-only angular-sector background texture for a Godot sky shader.
Primary request: Make ONE narrowly targeted refinement to the supplied generated sky image: remove the clouds that touch the outer left and right edges, and dissolve peripheral cloud wisps softly into blue sky across the outermost 12 percent on each side. Keep all main clouds, their detailed painterly interior shapes, the clear center-left opening, palette, lighting, image size and composition unchanged. This is still sky-only original artwork.
Exact change: the leftmost and rightmost 3 percent should contain ONLY open sky throughout the entire height, with a smooth matching blue-to-pale-cyan vertical atmospheric gradient. Across 3–12 percent in from either side, very sparse small wisps may appear and dissolve into the central image. Gently taper the peripheral cloud bases so none are clipped by either side border. Preserve every important cloud detail from the central 76 percent, particularly the luminous tall cumulus mass on the right and the medium warm cumulus on the left. The bottommost 10 percent remains calm pale cyan sky with no strong stripe; do not add a visible sea or land horizon.
Invariants: preserve the original 2:1 wide frame, keep all warm cream highlights and blue-lavender cloud undersides, keep the main right tower and center-left blue gap, keep the hand-painted fine designed brush planes and clear readable silhouettes. Native dimensions should be preserved; no upscale or extra texture noise.
Constraints: no land, water, sun disk, objects, birds, text, watermark, border, storm clouds or new cloud mass. This is one angular sector, not a 360-degree panorama.

calls.selection: Selected; visually inspected at native resolution and copied byte-for-byte to asset path.

preservation: Selected PNG copied byte-for-byte. No resize, color adjustment, manual painting, crop, recompression or pixel modification. Source and asset SHA-256 verified identical.

visual_review.subject: Sky and clouds only; no visible sun disk, land, sea, buildings, birds, text or objects.
visual_review.forms: Tall articulated warm cream cumulus tower on the right, medium-scale groups on the left, lavender-blue undersides and cohesive painted smaller lobes. Open airy blue gap spans center-left.
visual_review.edges: Extreme sides are predominantly open blue sky with cloud bases tapering inward. The second pass visibly removes edge-clipped clouds; a few tiny faint traces/wisps remain near the side margins. Exact edge or baseline color matching is not promised.
visual_review.horizon: Pale calm cyan-blue bottom, with faint low cloud streaks immediately above it; no land/sea boundary.
visual_review.resolution: Generator delivered 1774 x 887 despite requested 4096 x 2048. No upscale used. Angular-sector mapping provides a nominal 2.0–2.4x horizontal texel-density gain over mapping the original 1774px texture to 360 degrees.
visual_review.palette: Brighter/more saturated blue than the baseline, with warmer ivory cloud rims. Shader blending/tint should be assessed against the existing sky and scene.
mapping_limitations: Not a full equirectangular map and not a seamless repeating texture; do not wrap it over 360 degrees.
Intended center-left clear face opening uses approximate artwork UV x=0.28–0.47, y=0.32–0.65; camera placement may require sector rotation/vertical remapping.
Map from low horizon at artwork bottom to higher sky at top; vertical field of view is not calibrated and requires in-engine selection.
Blend sector side margins into the baseline rather than directly joining the two images. Opposite side colors are similar but not identical, and the baseline palette differs.
Only source image quality was inspected. Actual final-camera sharpness and cloud framing require an in-engine capture.

scope: Asset and provenance only. No shader, runtime, scene, material or import-setting changes. No GUI/browser interactions and no in-engine rendering done in this task.
